beats.narration: Begin by framing Course Purpose and Scope as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience. Consider this worked case: A student might develop a novel algorithm for data compression or design a prototype for a student-led tech startup. On screen, display a simple flowchart showing 'Student Idea' -> 'Faculty Sponsor' -> 'Independent Study' with arrows indicating mutual interest. List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion. This establishes the vocabulary and scope needed for the remaining sections.
beats.title: Course Purpose and Scope
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a simple flowchart showing 'Student Idea' -> 'Faculty Sponsor' -> 'Independent Study' with arrows indicating mutual interest.

beats.narration: Now define Proposal Drafting Process precisely enough that another learner could test the definition. A student works with a potential faculty sponsor to draft a proposal that describes what a student plans to do, what deliverables are expected, how the student's work will be evaluated, and how much credit will be assigned for successful completion of the work. Consider this worked case: The proposal specifies a three-month timeline, a working prototype as the deliverable, peer review as evaluation, and 3 credits for completion. On screen, show a template screenshot with labeled fields: 'Project Description', 'Deliverables', 'Evaluation Criteria', 'Credit Assignment'. Separate the formal definition from an implementation detail, then identify what evidence would distinguish them. A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
beats.title: Proposal Drafting Process
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a template screenshot with labeled fields: 'Project Description', 'Deliverables', 'Evaluation Criteria', 'Credit Assignment'.

beats.narration: With the foundation in place, examine how Faculty Sponsor Role operates in a concrete sequence. Students work with a supervising faculty member on topics of mutual interest. Consider this worked case: The sponsor provides technical feedback on the methodology and confirms that the project aligns with departmental resources. On screen, illustrate a handshake icon between 'Student' and 'Faculty Sponsor' with a checklist labeled 'Proposal Review'. Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition. The trace converts an abstract statement into an inspectable sequence. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Faculty Sponsor Role
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Illustrate a handshake icon between 'Student' and 'Faculty Sponsor' with a checklist labeled 'Proposal Review'.

beats.narration: Next, compare the choices involved in Grade Proposal Procedure and make the decision criteria explicit. The faculty sponsor proposes the grade, but before the grade is officially recorded, the student must submit a final report that summarizes what was actually accomplished. Consider this worked case: The sponsor recommends a B+ after reviewing the final deliverables, but the grade remains pending until the student submits the final report. On screen, display a timeline with two nodes: 'Grade Proposed' and 'Grade Officially Recorded', connected by an arrow labeled 'Final Report Submission'. Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts. Using shared criteria turns a preference into a defensible technical choice.
beats.title: Grade Proposal Procedure
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a timeline with two nodes: 'Grade Proposed' and 'Grade Officially Recorded', connected by an arrow labeled 'Final Report Submission'.

beats.narration: Apply Final Report Requirement to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition. They should respect privacy. Consider this worked case: The report includes a summary of tasks completed, challenges encountered, and evidence of deliverables meeting the proposed criteria. On screen, show a document icon with a checklist: 'Summary of Accomplishments', 'Deliverables Verification', 'Reflection on Process'. Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step. The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Final Report Requirement
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a document icon with a checklist: 'Summary of Accomplishments', 'Deliverables Verification', 'Reflection on Process'.

beats.narration: Examine the tradeoffs in Departmental Permission Requirement, including what improves and what becomes more difficult. Enrollment in this course requires permission from the department offering the course. Consider this worked case: The student submits a formal request to the CS department chair, who approves the enrollment based on academic standing and project feasibility. On screen, display a stamp graphic labeled 'Departmental Permission Granted' next to a course registration form. State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable. Making the tradeoff visible prevents a local improvement from hiding a larger cost.
beats.title: Departmental Permission Requirement
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a stamp graphic labeled 'Departmental Permission Granted' next to a course registration form.

beats.narration: Stress-test the reasoning around Ethical Standards in Independent Study with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome. Computing professionals should avoid harm. Consider this worked case: When developing a student tracking app, the student ensures data is anonymized and obtains informed consent from participants. On screen, show a shield icon with three sub-icons: 'Honesty', 'Privacy', 'Fairness', with a label 'Professional Ethics' above them. Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds. The edge case reveals the boundary of the claim without discarding the useful core idea.
beats.title: Ethical Standards in Independent Study
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a shield icon with three sub-icons: 'Honesty', 'Privacy', 'Fairness', with a label 'Professional Ethics' above them.

beats.narration: Use Research Integrity and Communication to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action. Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. Consider this worked case: The student's final report cites three relevant papers, reports test results without selective editing, and lists data collection constraints. On screen, display a document with callouts: 'Cite Prior Work', 'Report Results Accurately', 'Disclose Limitations'. Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause. The diagnosis is strongest when another person can reproduce the observation and the test. Name each dependency explicitly, and keep labels and representations consistent throughout the analysis.
beats.title: Research Integrity and Communication
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a document with callouts: 'Cite Prior Work', 'Report Results Accurately', 'Disclose Limitations'.

beats.narration: Connect Defining Verifiable Project Deliverables to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system. The proposal describes what the student plans to do, the expected deliverables, how the work will be evaluated, and the credit assigned for successful completion. Consider this worked case: A systems project names a working prototype, a reproducible evaluation with stated measures, and a final report as separate deliverables. On screen, show a project goal branching into three labeled deliverables: 'Working Artifact', 'Evaluation Evidence', and 'Final Report'. Explain how each deliverable supplies evidence for an evaluation criterion and verify that the proposed scope can be completed for the assigned credit. The synthesis matters only if every connection remains supported by the original proposal.
beats.title: Defining Verifiable Project Deliverables
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Show a project goal branching into three labeled deliverables: 'Working Artifact', 'Evaluation Evidence', and 'Final Report'.

beats.narration: Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Consider this worked case: The checklist confirms: proposal drafted, sponsor approved, deliverables defined, ethics reviewed, final report ready, and departmental permission secured. On screen, display a printable checklist with checkboxes for: 'Proposal Approved', 'Ethics Reviewed', 'Deliverables Defined', 'Final Report Ready', 'Permission Secured'. For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step. The result is a repeatable procedure, not a conclusion that depends on memory or intuition.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: template:academic-process | Display a printable checklist with checkboxes for: 'Proposal Approved', 'Ethics Reviewed', 'Deliverables Defined', 'Final Report Ready', 'Permission Secured'.

sources.excerpt: The ACM Code directs computing professionals to contribute to society and human well-being. Computing professionals should avoid harm. They should be honest and trustworthy. They should be fair and take action not to discriminate. They should respect the work required to produce new ideas and creative works. They should respect privacy. They should honor confidentiality. Professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products. They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice. Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate. Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.
sources.title: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct

sources.author: Association for Computing Machinery
sources.excerpt: Responsible technical communication distinguishes claims from evidence. It cites prior work and identifies the contribution being reported. Methods should be described well enough for readers to evaluate the work. Results should be reported accurately rather than selected to create a misleading conclusion. Limitations and threats to validity should be made visible. Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification. Conflicts and relevant relationships should be disclosed according to publication policy. A research project narrows a question, reviews literature, defines a reproducible method, evaluates results, and communicates for the intended audience.
